**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind readiness to the remote used by the ceremony**

When a checkout has multiple remotes—or `remote_name` is explicitly `null` despite an existing `origin`—these instructions allow the preflight to validate a different route from the one used later. The local `git remote get-url -h` confirms that `<name>` selects the queried remote, but steps 4c/5 subsequently re-probe and push hard-coded `origin` (`.aai/SKILL_PR.prompt.md:207,328`). Consequently readiness can return success without contacting the provider that will receive the push, allowing numbering and commits before the missing prerequisite is discovered. Require `origin` here or carry the selected remote consistently through the later platform and push commands.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Real finding, fixed in 609832744c202805234da8a09e40c5d3bb171308. Ceremony readiness now requires remote_name=origin when origin exists; null is permitted only when origin is absent, matching the later platform probes and push. TEST-006 failed before the instruction was added and now passes, including multiple-remotes/explicit-null controls and refusal snapshot preservation. RED/GREEN evidence: docs/ai/tdd/pr-capability-preflight-remediation-20261007/remote-red.log and preflight-green.log. Fresh native CI and independent validation/re-review are pending; this reply does not claim final merge readiness.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate origin's configured push URLs**

When `remote.origin.pushurl` differs from the fetch URL, or `origin` has multiple push URLs, this line validates only the fetch URL. `git remote get-url -h` explicitly documents `--push` as querying push URLs, while the ceremony later runs `git push -u origin <branch>` (`.aai/SKILL_PR.prompt.md:329`), which uses the configured push destination. Readiness can therefore verify repository A and then, after numbering and commits, push to repository B or fail there. Fresh evidence beyond the prior thread is the current implementation's omission of `--push` despite the remote-name fix; bind readiness to every actual push destination or refuse ambiguous configurations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Real finding, fixed in 627ee4449fe7fe46037ea92e1252832bfab1644f. Readiness now resolves effective fetch and push destinations through git remote get-url --all / --push --all, including pushInsteadOf, and refuses divergent or multiple endpoints before provider reads. TEST-001 first demonstrated expected refusal exit2 versus actual0, then passed divergent provider/repository, duplicate/multiple URLs and effective rewrite controls; ordinary and explicitly matching single destinations remain green. Evidence: docs/ai/tdd/pr-capability-preflight-pushurl-remediation-20261007T211358Z/pushurl-red.log and pushurl-preflight-green.log. New-source native run37690090374 and independent Validation/Review are pending. Lifecycle projection is causal evidence only; actual full-suite aggregate is not claimed green.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve remote URL whitespace until validation**

When a configured fetch/push URL has accidental leading or trailing whitespace, this `.trim()` removes it before `text()` and endpoint validation, so the preflight can probe the cleaned GitHub/Azure repository and report `READ_VERIFIED` even though the later `git push -u origin ...` uses the malformed configured URL. Fresh evidence beyond the fixed pushurl case: with Git 2.43.0, `git remote get-url --all` preserves a leading space and `git ls-remote origin` then fails with `protocol ' https' is not supported`; strip only Git's final line terminator so URL whitespace is rejected before ceremony writes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in aa18e55e44f9487f0b8fdb6093b5a587c789960a. TEST-001 now rejects effective fetch/push URL boundary spaces, tabs, CR and malformed multiline output before provider reads, while retaining lawful LF/CRLF and encoded-space/Unicode controls. Real pre-fix Git failures are classified product_red in docs/ai/tdd/pr-capability-preflight-final-remediation-20261007T224314Z/whitespace-red.log and terminator-CR-red.log; the final serial preflight passes all 8 rows (final-preflight-frozen-green.log). Git output delimiter is calibrated from rev-parse, so a URL trailing CR is not silently removed. Independent review and new native CI are in progress; no final Validation/merge-ready claim yet.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat empty push URLs as refused destinations**

On Git 2.43.0, an empty `remote.origin.pushurl` is emitted as an additional blank line by `git remote get-url --push --all` (`--push` queries push URLs and `--all` returns all URLs), and `git push` subsequently attempts that empty destination. The implementation therefore correctly returns `IDENTITY_INVALID`, while this new positive control expects `READ_VERIFIED`; running `bash .aai/scripts/aai-run-tests.sh bash tests/skills/test-aai-pr-preflight.sh test_001` fails at this assertion, so the current CI suite cannot pass. Make this a refusal case rather than claiming Git omits empty entries.

AGENTS.md reference: [.aai/AGENTS.md:L51-L57](https://github.com/goodwind-cz/aai/blob/aa18e55e44f9487f0b8fdb6093b5a587c789960a/.aai/AGENTS.md#L51-L57)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed the portable TEST-001 contract in bfea029b9a01d6a491d778f5bbf1ded5b3f2c88f. Reproduced with official real Git2.43: effective blank push destinations are emitted and the unchanged CLI correctly refuses them with IDENTITY_INVALID and zero provider calls. Git2.54 omits empty entries; the same controls verify the single lawful destination with three provider calls. Expectations now derive from independently captured effective Git bytes, with deterministic blank-first/last/only refusal controls. The CR fixtures also write quoted values and assert byte round-trip before invoking the CLI. Failing-first fixture proof: docs/ai/tdd/test008-native-20261008T000204Z/git243-before.red.log; GREEN on both versions: git243-final.log and host-final.log in that directory. SPEC blanket omission claim corrected with the existing owed signoff retained. Native TEST008 diagnostics remain pending; this does not claim PR readiness.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept GitHub's SSH-over-443 remote alias**

When `origin` uses [GitHub's documented SSH-over-HTTPS clone URL](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/troubleshooting-ssh/using-ssh-over-the-https-port), such as `ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/OWNER/REPO.git`, this unconditional port rejection returns `IDENTITY_INVALID` before any provider probe, even though the same remote remains valid for the ceremony's later `git push`. Handle the `ssh.github.com:443` transport alias and bind its provider checks to `github.com`; otherwise users who require SSH over port 443 cannot run `/aai-pr`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 5685e3625bc94f00ade55d9cf491158dde058177, regression TEST-007. Independent research and a maker failing-first test reproduced the documented ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443 alias being classified GitHub but refused by preflight before any provider call. The narrow fix recognizes that transport alias and binds provider read probes to github.com; literal single fetch/push destination equality remains required. GREEN verifies the exact three canonical-host probes and returned repository/hostname binding. Repository mismatch, divergent push destination, credentials and invalid ports still refuse. RED: docs/ai/tdd/test008-replay-20261008T010406Z/ssh443-red.log; GREEN: ssh443-green.log in that directory. Fresh independent Review and native CI are pending; no PR-readiness claim.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject passwords in SSH-over-443 remotes**

When `origin` is `ssh://git:secret@ssh.github.com:443/Org/Repo.git`, sanitizing before parsing erases `git:secret@`, so the preflight probes the canonical repository and reports `READ_VERIFIED`; the new TEST-007 password-bearing positive arm confirms this path. However, [Git's SSH URL syntax](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone#_git_urls) permits only `[user@]host[:port]`, and Git 2.43 passes this value to SSH as `git:secret@ssh.github.com:443` without `-p 443`, so the later `git push -u origin` in `.aai/SKILL_PR.prompt.md` cannot use the route that was verified. Parse the raw URL and reject a nonempty SSH password before applying output sanitization.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 1691558c034e13258a31b8288df5642f6263a8cb, regression TEST-007. Raw SSH authority is parsed before output sanitization; password-bearing SSH remotes refuse with IDENTITY_INVALID and zero provider calls. Independently checked in final parent Validation (2026-10-08T134948Z); all eight behavioral cases and twelve mutation replays pass. Exact-head native/full/docs CI at 9d90d1e4 is green.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse malformed scheme remotes before generic fallback**

When a scheme-based origin is malformed enough that `extractHost()` cannot parse it, this classifies it as `unknown` and the generic branch returns exit 0 without a provider call. For example, `https://github.com:bad/Org/Repo.git` produces `CAPABILITY_NOT_APPLICABLE`, although Git rejects the nonnumeric port; the ceremony can therefore perform numbering and close commits before the `git push -u origin` in `.aai/SKILL_PR.prompt.md` fails. Treat unparseable scheme URLs as `IDENTITY_INVALID` rather than as supported generic remotes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 6d3f616a96337ff1580968467fadfa9756a87a52, regression TEST-001 under SPEC-0211. Explicit scheme URLs are validated before provider classification and generic fallback. Nonnumeric GitHub and generic ports refuse with IDENTITY_INVALID and zero provider calls; lawful numeric generic remotes remain supported. Independently checked in final parent Validation (2026-10-08T134948Z); all eight behavioral cases and twelve mutation replays pass. Exact-head native/full/docs CI at 9d90d1e4 is green.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare GitHub repository identities case-insensitively**

When a valid origin uses different casing from GitHub's canonical repository name, such as `https://github.com/goodwind-cz/aai.git` while `gh repo view` returns `goodwind-cz/AAI`, GitHub resolves the same repository and Git transport remains usable, but these exact comparisons return `PROVIDER_RESULT_INVALID`. Normalize the owner/name and returned URL path for GitHub's case-insensitive identity semantics before comparing them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in bddaa7657ac0c92dc22f0bc25d4bff7df22cf91c, regression TEST-007 under SPEC-0212. GitHub owner/repository, nameWithOwner and returned URL paths compare ASCII case-insensitively. Actual mismatches and Unicode confusables still refuse; fetch/push endpoint equality remains byte-exact and actual provider spelling is preserved in argv. Independently checked in final parent Validation (2026-10-08T134948Z); all eight behavioral cases and twelve mutation replays pass. Exact-head native/full/docs CI at 9d90d1e4 is green.
